newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria journalists sentenced over death report.
newsitem.headline: Algeria journalists sentenced over death report.

text.p: An Algerian court has passed suspended jail sentences on an influential Algerian newspaper director and five other journalists for "prematurely" reporting the killing of five gendarmes in 1993.
An Algiers court on Wednesday sentenced Omar Belhouchet, director of El Watan, and Nacera Benali who wrote the report, to six months' imprisonment, El Watan said on Thursday.
Four other journalists working for the newspaper each received four-month terms. All sentences were suspended, the paper added.

Belhouchet's French-language newspaper, viewed as the best informed on security issues in the violence-ridden country, reported in January 1993 that an armed group had cut the throats of five gendarmes in Ksar El Hirane, in Laghouat province some 350 km (220 miles) south of Algiers.
He and the staff members were charged with "premature publication" and other offences, including threatening state security.
They were arrested and held for several days in Serkadji high security prison. El Watan was suspended for a week.
Belhouchet has been charged several times by Algerian authorities who have draconian powers over the media. He also survived an attempt to kill him which officials blamed on Moslem fundamentalists.

At least 60 Algerian journalists or media employees have been killed since May 1993, caught up in the conflict between the authorities and the fundamentalists. The first to die was Tahar Djaoud, gunned down in his car on May 26. He died eight days later.
Subjected to tough censorship, particularly on security matters, the journalists are accused by Moslem guerrillas of siding with the authorities by not reporting rebel "successes".
Under Algerian law, "apology for terrorism", "threatening state security" and "undermining state institutions" are punishable by jail terms. They are open to wide interpretation.

Many of Algeria's newspapers have been suspended for various periods since violence erupted after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election dominated by the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS).
